started: You moved a colleague to the desk with no window, so that you could say who sat where.

outcomes.playedOut: The colleague by the printer turned out to sit on the Health and Safety committee. They came looking for something to hold against you, and you had sat through your one training module properly. It cost you only a form.

bill.title: FW: Health and Safety Committee
bill.body: It turns out that the colleague you moved beside the printer sits on the Health and Safety committee. The committee has reviewed your training record, and can find nothing wrong with it. It has asked you to fill in a form confirming this, in triplicate, by the printer.

gauges.note: The desk with no window came back, and you had done the training. It cost you a form.

outcomes.playedOut: The colleague by the printer turned out to sit on the Health and Safety committee. Months after the desk, they called you out for never putting your team through safety training.

bill.from: From: The Health and Safety Committee
bill.title: Your team's safety training is overdue
bill.body: It turns out that the colleague you moved beside the printer sits on the Health and Safety committee. They have looked up your team, and nobody on it has done any safety training. Neither have you. The committee has copied your boss, and would like to know what you propose.

options.label: Book the whole team in, and go first

result.title: Fire Marshal Awareness
result.body: You spend a morning learning which way the doors open. The committee marks the action as closed, and the colleague by the printer looks across at you, and does not need to say anything.

options.label: Reply that it was already scheduled, and attach a schedule

result.title: The schedule
result.body: You make the schedule that afternoon. The committee thanks you, and points out that the date you chose was a Sunday. It has noted this as well.

escapes.label: Say the Office Co-ordinator holds the training records

worked.body: The committee writes to the Office Co-ordinator about the training records, which are in a drawer, as records are.
worked.reported: Training records were found to be held locally, and will be digitised.
worked.happened: You said the Office Co-ordinator had the training records. There were no records.

failed.body: The Office Co-ordinator sends the committee the drawer's contents: a form for each of the team, unsigned, with your name at the top as the person to chase them.

escapes.label: Answer the committee

gauges.note: The desk with no window came back, and the committee had you on the training.

started: In the Lessons Learned Review, you took the blame for something, and the minutes recorded it.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone in that review remembered who had taken the blame. When your project next needed something, it arrived, and nobody asked for a form.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Something for your project
bill.body: The figures your project has been waiting for since the spring are on your desk. There is no note. The Senior Analyst was in the review where you took the blame, and walks past without looking up, which you are starting to recognise as a form of respect.

gauges.note: You took the blame in the review, and it came back as figures on your desk.

started: You made your project green in the Monthly Status Report, when it was not.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone from Finance set your green report beside the real figures, and took the two of them to your boss, who believed in reports. It went on your file as a big mistake.

bill.from: From: Finance, copied to your boss
bill.title: A small discrepancy
bill.body: Someone in Finance, whom you have never met, has been reading old Monthly Status Reports for pleasure. They have laid one of your green ones beside the figures, and sent both to your boss, with no comment. Your boss has read them both, properly.

gauges.note: The green report came back, and Finance believed it.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone from Finance set your green report beside the real figures. It went nowhere much: your boss had signed the same report, and preferred it left alone.

bill.from: From: Finance, copied to your boss
bill.title: A small discrepancy
bill.body: Someone in Finance, whom you have never met, has been reading old Monthly Status Reports for pleasure. They have laid one of your green ones beside the figures, and sent both to your boss. Your boss replies to all, thanking Finance for its engagement. You are not to do it again, or at least not in writing.

escapes.label: Say the Project Co-ordinator put that month's report together

worked.body: Finance thanks the Project Co-ordinator for their engagement. The Project Co-ordinator does not know what they did.
worked.reported: A reporting discrepancy was traced to how the report was put together.
worked.happened: You said the Project Co-ordinator wrote your green report. It had your name in the footer.

failed.body: The Project Co-ordinator replies with the file's properties. Author: you. Last modified: you, at eleven at night.

escapes.label: Reply that green was the forecast, not the status

worked.body: Finance replies that forecasting is outside its remit, and closes the query.
worked.reported: A status report was clarified as a forecast.
worked.happened: You said your green status had been a forecast. It had been a wish.

failed.body: Your boss was in the meeting where you said it was green now, not later, and replies to all to say so.

escapes.label: Reply to all, thanking Finance for its engagement

gauges.note: The green report came back, and it had your name on it.

started: You decided who got the bonus pot, and the people who did not get it could count.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator remembered who had got the bonus pot, and your figures began to arrive late, with apologies.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Apologies for the delay
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator is very sorry that your figures are late. They have been very busy doing the work. They mention this twice, and look at your new chair while they do.

escapes.label: Ask the Project Co-ordinator for a delivery plan for the figures

worked.body: The Project Co-ordinator sends a delivery plan, which takes them a week, so the figures are later still, but now on a plan.
worked.reported: Late figures were brought under a delivery plan.
worked.happened: You buried the late figures under a plan for them.

failed.body: The delivery plan has a section headed Dependencies, and the dependency is a chair.
failed.why: The Project Co-ordinator had already gone off you, and the delivery plan said so.

escapes.label: Wait for the figures

gauges.note: The bonus pot came back, and it was remembered who decided it.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator remembered who had shared out the bonus pot, and why, and stayed late on your project without being asked.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Done, by the way
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator has stayed late and sorted out the part of your project that nobody wanted. The email is one line long. Nobody on this floor has ever sent you a one-line email that was good news.

gauges.note: The bonus pot came back, as a favour returned.

started: You blamed a colleague in front of the floor, and the floor talks.

outcomes.playedOut: What you had done reached the Office Co-ordinator, who keeps the room bookings. Your meetings began to be in a different room from the one on the invitation.

bill.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
bill.title: Room change
bill.body: Your one o'clock has been moved. Nobody can find the message that said so, though the Office Co-ordinator is quite sure that one was sent. By the time you arrive, it has finished, and it went very well.

gauges.note: Blaming a colleague came back on them, and not on you.

started: You went to a meeting, and somebody took minutes.

outcomes.playedOut: The Office Co-ordinator, who thought well of you, wrote the minutes of that meeting. Months later they were circulated, and they were kind.

bill.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
bill.title: Minutes: for information
bill.body: The Office Co-ordinator has circulated the minutes of a meeting you went to months ago. They record that you made a valuable contribution. You did not speak. Your boss has read them, and has started nodding at you in the corridor.

gauges.note: The minutes of an old meeting came back, and were kind to you.

outcomes.playedOut: Months after the meeting, its minutes were circulated, and they had an action against your name that nobody remembered agreeing.

bill.from: From: The shared calendar
bill.title: Action: you (from the minutes)
bill.body: The minutes of a meeting you went to months ago have been circulated at last. They record an action against your name: to take forward the cross-team synergy piece. Nobody remembers agreeing it, including you, but it is minuted, and minutes are how things happen here.

escapes.label: Say the action was meant for the Junior Associate

worked.body: The Junior Associate accepts the cross-team synergy piece, and asks you what it is. You say it is a development opportunity.
worked.reported: The synergy action was reassigned as a development opportunity.
worked.happened: You gave the Junior Associate an action nobody had agreed to.

failed.body: The Junior Associate replies to all, asking what meeting it was, and who was at it. The minutes say who was. It was you.

escapes.label: Reply to all, asking whether this is the latest version of the minutes

worked.body: Three versions of the minutes go round in reply. In two of them the action has nobody's name on it.
worked.reported: The minutes were revised following comments.
worked.happened: You asked which version was the latest, until there was one without your name.

failed.body: Someone replies with the final version, which is marked Final, and has your name in bold.

escapes.label: Take the action forward

gauges.note: The minutes of an old meeting came back with an action against your name.

started: In the Monthly Alignment Meeting, you agreed warmly with one of your managers.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss passed your warm agreement up a floor, as proof that the team was aligned, and it came back down with your name on it.

bill.from: From: Floor 2, copied to you
bill.title: FW: FW: FW: the view from the ground
bill.body: Your boss's boss has told Floor 2 that the team is fully aligned, and given you as the example. Floor 2 has replied with a thumbs-up, from someone whose title has the word Chief in it twice. You have printed it out, and you are not sure where to put it.

gauges.note: Agreeing warmly with your boss's boss went up a floor, with your name on it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss repeated your warm agreement upstairs, as proof that they had their team behind them, and it came back down with your name on it.

bill.from: From: Floor 2, copied to you
bill.title: RE: who is behind this?
bill.body: Your boss has told Floor 2 that the team is right behind them, and named you, as the team. Floor 2 has asked who you are. Your boss has replied with a photograph of you agreeing, which you did not know had been taken.

gauges.note: Agreeing warmly with your boss went up a floor, with your name on it.

started: At the Town Hall, you sat next to one of your managers and were seen agreeing with them.

outcomes.playedOut: A colleague set your warm agreement with your boss beside your nodding at your boss's boss, who wanted the opposite, and sent the two round.

bill.from: From: A colleague on the fourth floor
bill.title: Spot the difference
bill.body: A colleague you have never met has sent the whole floor two photographs. In one, you agree warmly with your boss. In the other, you nod beside your boss's boss, who is saying the opposite. The subject line is Spot the difference. Nineteen people have replied with the answer, which is you.

gauges.note: You were caught agreeing with your boss, then nodding along with your boss's boss on the other side.

outcomes.playedOut: A colleague set your warm agreement with your boss's boss beside your laughing along with your boss, who wanted the opposite, and sent the two round.

bill.from: From: A colleague on the fourth floor
bill.title: Spot the difference
bill.body: A colleague you have never met has sent the whole floor two photographs. In one, you agree warmly with your boss's boss. In the other, you laugh beside your boss, at a joke about synergy. The subject line is Spot the difference. Nineteen people have replied with the answer, which is you.

gauges.note: You were caught agreeing with your boss's boss, then laughing along with your boss on the other side.

outcomes.playedOut: The Town Hall's photographer caught you nodding beside your boss's boss, and the picture went on the intranet.

bill.from: From: Internal Communications
bill.title: Our people: a picture says it all
bill.body: The front page of the intranet has a new picture, under the heading Our people. It shows your boss's boss at the Town Hall, and beside them, nodding, you. Your boss's boss has asked Internal Communications for a copy, in a frame.

gauges.note: Nodding beside your boss's boss at the Town Hall made the front page of the intranet.

outcomes.playedOut: The recording of the Town Hall caught you laughing along with your boss, and it was used to show what engagement looks like.

bill.from: From: Internal Communications
bill.title: New module: What Engagement Looks Like
bill.body: The new mandatory module on engagement has a clip from the Town Hall. It shows your boss laughing at the joke about synergy, and you laughing half a second later, every time. The voice-over calls this active listening. Your boss has watched it twice, and sent it to their boss.

gauges.note: Laughing along with your boss at the Town Hall ended up in a training module.

started: In the Quarterly Business Review, you said your team's arrow was all down to one of your managers.

outcomes.playedOut: Floor 2 traced the arrow you gave away back to your green Monthly Status Report, and the credit came back to you with the blame attached.

bill.from: From: Floor 2
bill.title: Returned to sender
bill.body: Floor 2 has looked into the arrow you said was all down to leadership. It was drawn from one of your green Monthly Status Reports. Leadership has politely declined the credit, and returned it to you, with the arrow, in an envelope marked Not for us.

gauges.note: You gave the credit for an arrow from your green report away, and it was sent back.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss put your line on a slide of their own, and the slide said who had said it first.

bill.from: From: Floor 2, copied to you
bill.title: Deck: Leadership Offsite (draft 4)
bill.body: Your boss's boss has a new slide for the Leadership Offsite. It says All down to leadership, in large type, and underneath, in very small type, a quote from you. Floor 2 has asked who you are, and your boss's boss has told them.

gauges.note: Handing the arrow to your boss's boss was noticed, with your name on it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss put the arrow in their own summary for upstairs, and upstairs found the minutes that said who had given it to them.

bill.from: From: Floor 2, copied to you
bill.title: Thank you for your generosity of spirit
bill.body: Your boss has written up the arrow for Floor 2 as personally delivered. Floor 2 read the minutes of the Quarterly Business Review, found who had said so first, and has written to thank you for your generosity of spirit. Your boss has been copied, and has started saying good morning to you by name.

gauges.note: Handing the arrow to your boss was noticed, with your name on it.

started: You stayed late to make everything in your boss's slides fly in.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's slides froze upstairs on the one where the word Growth spins, and the file had your name on it.

bill.from: From: IT Services
bill.title: Incident report: boardroom projector
bill.body: Upstairs, your boss's slides froze on the one where the word Growth spins in. Growth kept spinning. Your boss presented the rest from memory, beside it. IT Services has traced the file to you, and asks that nothing be made to fly in again without a change request.

gauges.note: The slides you made fly in for your boss froze upstairs, with Growth spinning.

started: You suggested that the bonus pot should go to your boss, for leadership.

outcomes.playedOut: Human Resources took your bonus pot recommendation as a nomination, and your boss was shortlisted with your name on the form.

bill.from: From: Human Resources
bill.title: Nomination received: Leader of the Year
bill.body: Human Resources thanks you for nominating your boss for Leader of the Year, which it turns out your bonus pot recommendation did. Your boss has been shortlisted. The form has your name at the top as nominator, and your boss has read it several times.

gauges.note: Suggesting the bonus pot go to your boss came back as a nomination, with your name on it.

started: You spent the underspend on something large, where upstairs would see it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss showed a visitor the forty chairs as an investment in people, and the caption gave your name.

bill.from: From: Internal Communications
bill.title: Investing in our people
bill.body: Your boss's boss walked a visitor from head office past the forty new chairs in the corridor, said that they were an investment in people, and sat in one for a photograph. The caption on the intranet names you as the person behind the investment. Facilities would still like a receipt.

gauges.note: The forty chairs in the corridor were seen upstairs, and sat in.

started: You hired your old friend onto your team, over the candidate the Senior Analyst recommended.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss believed in doing the job, and found out that your old friend could not. They were furious, and said so, slowly.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: A word about your new hire
bill.body: Your boss has asked to see you about your new hire, who has been asked three times what they do and has given three answers, all of them transformation. Your boss is not angry. Your boss has used the word appalled, and spelt it out.

options.label: Say that it was your mistake, and that you will put it right

result.title: Your new hire
result.body: Your boss says that it took something to say so, and asks when it will be put right by. The answer your boss wants is soon.

options.label: Say that your friend is still onboarding

result.title: Your new hire
result.body: Your boss asks how long onboarding takes. You say that it varies. Your boss writes down the date.

options.label: Do your friend's work yourself until they learn it

result.title: Your new hire
result.body: You do two jobs, one of them in your friend's name. Your friend's work improves markedly, and your friend is very pleased with it.

escapes.label: Say the Senior Analyst signed off the interview panel

worked.body: Your boss asks the Senior Analyst why they signed it off. The Senior Analyst, who did not, is now very careful near your desk.
worked.reported: The sign-off of recruitment panels is under review.
worked.happened: You said the Senior Analyst signed off your friend's hire. They had recommended someone else.

failed.body: The Senior Analyst sends your boss the e-mail recommending the other candidate, with your reply, which was a thumbs-up.

escapes.label: Go and see your boss

gauges.note: Your old friend came back on you, in your boss's office.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss worked out how your old friend had been hired, and kept it, for later.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: About your new hire
bill.body: Your boss lets it be known that they know how your new hire came to be hired, and that it can stay between the two of you. For now. Your boss starts a sentence with you owe me, and leaves it there.

escapes.label: Say the hire went through a proper panel

worked.body: Your boss says that of course it did, and lets it go, and does not write that down.
worked.reported: A hire was confirmed as made through due process.
worked.happened: You told your boss there had been a panel. There had been a coffee.

failed.body: Your boss asks for the panel's notes. There are none. Your boss lets it be known that this, too, can stay between the two of you.
failed.why: Your boss had already gone off you, and asked for the notes.

escapes.label: Say nothing

gauges.note: Your old friend came back, as something your boss keeps.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss could not tell what your old friend did, and liked them for agreeing with everything.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: Great hire
bill.body: Your boss has noticed your new hire, who agrees with everything your boss says, often before your boss has finished saying it. Your boss calls it a great hire. Your team is doing your friend's work.

gauges.note: Your old friend came back, as a great hire, and the work went elsewhere.

started: You spent your team's transformation budget on an expensive consultant.

outcomes.playedOut: The consultant presented their findings. Your boss asked what they meant, and then what they had cost.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: The consultant's readout
bill.body: The consultant presents their findings: that your team should keep doing what it was doing, but transformationally. Your boss asks what that means, twice, and then asks what it cost.

escapes.label: Say the Programme Manager chose the consultant

worked.body: Your boss writes to the Programme Manager about value for money. The Programme Manager adds it to the lessons log.
worked.reported: Lessons about value for money were logged for the transformation budget.
worked.happened: You said the Programme Manager chose the consultant. You chose them at the coffee machine.

failed.body: The Programme Manager sends your boss the purchase order, which you raised, and the meeting invite, which you sent.

escapes.label: Say the readout proves the team was right all along, which is value

worked.body: Your boss says that confirmation is valuable, and writes it on a slide.
worked.reported: The consultancy confirmed the team's direction.
worked.happened: You said that paying to be told you were right was value.

failed.body: Your boss sat through the whole readout, and asks how much it cost to be told that.

escapes.label: Say what it cost

gauges.note: The consultant came back, as a question about what it cost.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst remembered whose spreadsheet the consultant's framework was, and showed your boss the version history.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Version history
bill.body: The Senior Analyst has sent your boss their spreadsheet from last spring, which is the consultant's framework, with the version history attached. The colours are different. Nothing else is.

escapes.label: Say the framework is an industry standard, and both of them used it

worked.body: Your boss accepts that frameworks are industry standard. The Senior Analyst adds a footnote to theirs: industry standard since last spring.
worked.reported: The consultancy used a framework that is standard in the industry.
worked.happened: You said the Senior Analyst's spreadsheet was an industry standard. It is now.

failed.body: Your boss saw the Senior Analyst's spreadsheet last spring, and liked it then too.

escapes.label: Thank the Senior Analyst for the version history

gauges.note: The consultant came back, as somebody else's spreadsheet.

outcomes.playedOut: The consultant presented their findings, which were nothing, and your boss was impressed by them.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: The consultant's readout
bill.body: Your boss was in the room for the consultant's readout, and has asked for a copy of the deck and the consultant's number. The consultant recommends a second phase. Your boss would like to sponsor it.

gauges.note: The consultant came back, and your boss was impressed by it.

started: You divided your team's bonus pot, and signed every letter.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst remembered their letter about resilience, and began to do exactly what was asked, and no more.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Open to opportunities
bill.body: The Senior Analyst's profile now says Open to Opportunities. They are still doing the work, to the letter, and the letter is shorter than it was. Whoever had the bonus has asked them how to do it.

escapes.label: Ask People and Culture to run an engagement survey

worked.body: The survey runs for six weeks. Its results are shown as a word cloud, and the biggest word is Valued.
worked.reported: Team engagement was measured, and found to be valued.
worked.happened: You buried a resignation in a survey.

failed.body: The survey's free-text box has one answer in it, very long, from the Senior Analyst.

escapes.label: Let it be

gauges.note: Your team's bonus pot came back, and it was remembered who signed the letters.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator pinned their letter about resilience where your boss would read it.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Resilience
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator has pinned your letter about resilience above their desk. Your boss has read it there, and asked the Project Co-ordinator how they are, and been told.

escapes.label: Say the letter was People and Culture's template

worked.body: Your boss nods at People and Culture's template. People and Culture are asked to make the template warmer.
worked.reported: Bonus letter templates are to be reviewed for tone.
worked.happened: You said People and Culture wrote your letter about resilience. You wrote it.

failed.body: Your boss signed off the letter, and remembers the word resilience, underlined, in your handwriting.

escapes.label: Leave the letter where it is

gauges.note: Your team's bonus pot came back, pinned above a desk.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst remembered why they had the biggest share of the bonus pot, and closed the oldest item on your project's risk log.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Closed
bill.body: The Senior Analyst has closed the oldest item on your project's risk log, which was open before you joined. They mention it to nobody, and your boss hears of it anyway.

gauges.note: Your team's bonus pot came back, as work done.

started: You moved the Project Co-ordinator to the desk by the lift, for questioning your plans.

outcomes.playedOut: From the desk by the lift, the Project Co-ordinator met everyone who came up, your boss included, and told them how your team was doing.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Good morning
bill.body: From the desk by the lift, the Project Co-ordinator says good morning to everyone who comes up to Floor 2, your boss included. Your boss now hears how your team is doing before you do, and in more detail.

escapes.label: Say the Office Co-ordinator put them by the lift

worked.body: Your boss asks the Office Co-ordinator about the desk by the lift. The Office Co-ordinator says it is a temporary arrangement, which here means the opposite.
worked.reported: The desk by the lift is a temporary arrangement.
worked.happened: You said the Office Co-ordinator moved the Project Co-ordinator. You did.

failed.body: The Office Co-ordinator sends your boss the request to move the desk. It is from you, and the reason given is Questions.

escapes.label: Say good morning back

gauges.note: The desk by the lift came back, every morning, at the lift.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator made the desk by the lift their own, and became the person the floor asks.

bill.title: The desk by the lift
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator has made the desk by the lift their own. There is a plant, and a sign-in sheet, and visitors ask them where things are. It is the busiest desk on the floor.

gauges.note: The desk by the lift came back, as a plant and a sign-in sheet.

started: You took the Board's question about slide seven offline.

outcomes.playedOut: The Board wanted its answer offline, in writing, and asked for it.

bill.from: From: The Board Office
bill.title: Your offline answer
bill.body: The Board is still waiting for the answer to the question about slide seven, which you took offline. It would like the answer before the next Board, so that it can be taken offline again if necessary.

options.label: Reply that you are still taking it offline

result.title: Your offline answer
result.body: The Board Office notes your update, and puts the question on the agenda of the next Board, as item one.

options.label: Find the real answer, and send it

result.title: Your offline answer
result.body: It takes two days, and it is a less good figure than anyone hoped. The Board Office thanks you for it, and files it with the question.

escapes.label: Reply that the answer is with a working group

worked.body: The Board Office adds the working group to its list of things to chase. The working group does not exist, which makes it hard to chase.
worked.reported: The answer on slide seven is with a working group.
worked.happened: You made up a working group to have the answer.

failed.body: The Board Office asks for the working group's terms of reference, its members and its chair, which it suggests should be you.

escapes.label: Answer the Board Office

gauges.note: The question you took offline came back, as item one.

started: You passed the Chief Financial Officer's thirty per cent down to your team.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst lost a contractor to your cut, and did seventy per cent of everything from then on, labelled.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Seventy per cent
bill.body: Since the cut, the Senior Analyst does exactly seventy per cent of everything, and labels it: a report seventy per cent long, a meeting left at minute forty-two. It is very precise, and your boss has noticed the labels.

escapes.label: Say seventy per cent is the team's new efficiency target

worked.body: Your boss is impressed by the target, and asks whether the rest of the floor could hit seventy per cent too.
worked.reported: The team piloted an efficiency target of seventy per cent.
worked.happened: You said the Senior Analyst's protest was a target.

failed.body: Your boss read the Chief Financial Officer's e-mail about the cut, and the labels say the same thing.

escapes.label: Say nothing about the labels

gauges.note: The cut you passed down came back, at seventy per cent.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator lost their training to your cut, and started a lunchtime session about how budgets are cut.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Self-directed learning
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator, whose training went in your cut, has started a lunchtime session called Self-Directed Learning. It is very well attended. This week's topic is how a cut is passed down, with worked examples.

escapes.label: Book the room at the same lunchtime, for a mandatory briefing

worked.body: Your briefing takes the room. Self-Directed Learning moves to the stairwell, where attendance is lower and the acoustics better.
worked.reported: A mandatory briefing was well attended.
worked.happened: You took the room away from a session about you.

failed.body: Self-Directed Learning moves to your briefing, and asks questions.

escapes.label: Attend

gauges.note: The cut you passed down came back, at lunchtime.

outcomes.playedOut: Your team absorbed the cut, and said nothing, which was noticed upstairs as resilience.

bill.title: Absorbed
bill.body: Your team has absorbed thirty per cent, and is now described upstairs as lean. Two of them have updated their profiles online.

gauges.note: The cut you passed down came back, as somebody's resilience.

started: You had your team write the Board's offsite deck overnight.

outcomes.playedOut: The Junior Associate wrote slide forty overnight, and told your boss's boss so, in the lift.

bill.from: From: The Junior Associate, Tessa Croft
bill.title: Slide forty
bill.body: The Junior Associate has mentioned to your boss's boss, in the lift, that they wrote slide forty of the offsite deck, at five in the morning. Your boss's boss had particularly liked slide forty, and had told you so, and you had said thank you.

escapes.label: Tell your boss's boss that you wrote it, and the Junior Associate typed it up

worked.body: Your boss's boss says that is how it should work: the thinking at your level, the typing below.
worked.reported: Slide forty was developed by the team lead and formatted by the team.
worked.happened: You said you wrote slide forty. You were asleep.

failed.body: Your boss was copied on the e-mail at five in the morning, with slide forty attached, from the Junior Associate.

escapes.label: Thank the Junior Associate, in the lift

gauges.note: The deck your team wrote overnight came back, in the lift.

outcomes.playedOut: The Junior Associate wrote the offsite deck overnight, and their out-of-office said so.

bill.from: From: The Junior Associate, Tessa Croft
bill.title: Out of office
bill.body: The Junior Associate's out-of-office says that they are recovering from writing the Board's offsite deck overnight, and that questions about it should go to you. Your boss has had the out-of-office twice.

escapes.label: Ask IT to switch off the out-of-office

worked.body: IT switches it off, and asks if there is anything else. There is not, any more.
worked.reported: An out-of-office message was corrected.
worked.happened: You had an out-of-office switched off because it was true.

failed.body: IT switches it off, and the Junior Associate switches it back on, with a sentence added about IT.

escapes.label: Answer the questions about the deck

gauges.note: The deck your team wrote overnight came back, as an out-of-office.

outcomes.playedOut: Your team's overnight deck became Floor 3's template, and your team the people who write it.

bill.title: The template
bill.body: Your team's offsite deck is now the template for every offsite on Floor 3. Your team has been asked to write next year's, by next week.

gauges.note: The deck your team wrote overnight came back, as a template.

started: You put in writing what the Chief Financial Officer's cut would stop.

outcomes.playedOut: The Chief Financial Officer's office sent your list round Floor 3 as an example, and the things on it stopped.

bill.title: The two pages
bill.body: The Chief Financial Officer's office has sent your list of what will stop to every manager on Floor 3, as an example. Three of the things on it have stopped, officially, which nobody on Floor 3 can remember happening before.

gauges.note: The list of what your cut would stop came back, as an example.

started: You told the Board that you did not know, and when you would.

outcomes.playedOut: The Board had its answer when you said it would, and asked for every answer from Floor 3 to come with a date.

bill.from: From: The Board Office
bill.title: Friday
bill.body: The Board had your figure on Friday, as you said it would. The Chair of the Board has asked that every answer from Floor 3 come with a date like that one. Floor 3 is not pleased with you about this, and your boss's boss is.

gauges.note: The answer you gave the Board by Friday came back, as a rule.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss sent the Board your figure on Friday, under their own name.

bill.from: From: Your boss, {boss}
bill.title: Friday
bill.body: Your boss has sent the Board your figure on Friday, as promised, from their own address, with a note about how hard Floor 3 has been working on it. You are copied in, at the bottom.

escapes.label: Forward the Board your own e-mail of the figure, dated Thursday

worked.body: The Board Office files both. Someone there notices that one is dated Thursday, and mentions it to someone upstairs.
worked.reported: The Board received the figure on time, twice.
worked.happened: You made sure the Board saw who sent it first.

failed.body: Your boss is copied, and replies to you alone, with one word: Noted.

escapes.label: Leave it under your boss's name

gauges.note: The answer you gave the Board came back, under someone else's name.

started: You forecast what you actually expected, which was lower.

outcomes.playedOut: Your forecast was the only one on Floor 3 that came true.

bill.title: The forecast that came true
bill.body: The quarter is in, and yours was the only forecast on Floor 3 that came true. The Chief Financial Officer's office has asked you to do everyone's next time, and everyone else has heard.

gauges.note: The forecast you made honestly came back true.

started: You said at the Team Structure Review what each of your team does, and that you need all of them.

outcomes.playedOut: Your team heard what you had said at the Team Structure Review.

bill.title: What you said
bill.body: Your team has heard what you said about each of them at the Team Structure Review, from someone who was there. Nobody mentions it. The Senior Analyst brings you a coffee, which has not happened before.

remembers.text: You said what they do, and that you need them, at the Team Structure Review.
You said what they do, and that you need them, at the Team Structure Review.

gauges.note: What you said for your team came back, as a coffee.

started: You put your figure down to the Senior Analyst, in front of the Board.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst sent the Board Office the workings behind the figure you had put down to them, with the date they had sent them to you.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: The workings
bill.body: The Senior Analyst has sent the Board Office the workings behind the figure on slide seven, which you said came from them. The workings have a date on them, and the date is three weeks before the Board, and the e-mail they came in was to you.

escapes.label: Say the workings were sent to you to check, not written for you

worked.body: The Board Office accepts that you were checking. It asks whether checking is the same as getting it wrong, and decides not to find out.
worked.reported: A Board figure was confirmed as checked by the team lead.
worked.happened: You said you had only been checking the Senior Analyst's workings. They were the figure.

failed.body: Your boss was copied on the e-mail with the workings, and the Board Office has asked your boss.

escapes.label: Correct the record

gauges.note: The figure you put down to the Senior Analyst came back, with its workings.

outcomes.playedOut: The Senior Analyst let it go, and kept the e-mail.

bill.title: Slide seven
bill.body: Nobody mentions slide seven again. The Senior Analyst now copies you into everything, with the date in the subject line.

gauges.note: The figure you put down to the Senior Analyst came back, as dates in subject lines.
